title: Investigating Endocrine Disrupting Impacts of Nine Disinfection Byproducts on Human and Zebrafish Estrogen Receptor Alpha.
authors: Lee, Sang-Ah; Park, Chang Gyun; Esterhuizen, Maranda; Choi, Ian; Ryu, Chang Seon; Yang, Ji Hun; Kim, Young Jun
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过报告基因实验和分子对接比较九种消毒副产物对人及斑马鱼雌激素受体α的激动/拮抗作用，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作建模，但对象为小分子-核受体而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Disinfection byproducts (DBPs) cause endocrine disruption via estrogenic or anti-estrogenic effects on estrogen receptors. However, most studies have focused on human systems, with little experimental data being presented on aquatic biota. This study aimed to compare the effects of nine DBPs on zebrafish and human estrogen receptor alpha (zERalpha and hERalpha). METHODS: In vitro enzyme response-based tests, including cytotoxicity and reporter gene assays, were performed. Additionally, statistical analysis and molecular docking studies were employed to compare ERalpha responses. RESULTS: Iodoacetic acid (IAA), chloroacetonitrile (CAN), and bromoacetonitrile (BAN) showed robust estrogenic activity on hERalpha(maximal induction ratios of 108.7%, 50.3%, and 54.7%, respectively), while IAA strongly inhibited the estrogenic activity induced by 17beta-estradiol (E2) in zERalpha (59.8% induction at the maximum concentration). Chloroacetamide (CAM) and bromoacetamide (BAM) also showed robust anti-estrogen effects in zERalpha (48.1% and 50.8% induction at the maximum concentration, respectively). These dissimilar endocrine disruption patterns were thoroughly assessed using Pearson correlation and distance-based analyses. Clear differences between the estrogenic responses of the two ERalphas were observed, whereas no pattern of anti-estrogenic activities could be established. Some DBPs strongly induced estrogenic endocrine disruption as agonists of hERalpha, while others inhibited estrogenic activity as antagonists of zERalpha. Principal coordinate analysis (PCoA) showed similar correlation coefficients for estrogenic and anti-estrogenic responses. Reproducible results were obtained from computational analysis and the reporter gene assay. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the effects of DBPs on both human and zebrafish highlight the importance of controlling their differences in responsiveness for estrogenic activities including the water quality monitoring and endocrine disruption, as DBPs have species-specific ligand-receptor interactions.
abstract_zh: 背景：消毒副产物（DBPs）通过雌激素受体上的雌激素或抗雌激素效应引起内分泌干扰。然而，大多数研究集中于人类系统，关于水生生物的实验数据很少。本研究旨在比较九种DBPs对斑马鱼和人类雌激素受体α（zERalpha和hERalpha）的影响。方法：进行了基于体外酶反应的测试，包括细胞毒性和报告基因检测。此外，采用统计分析和分子对接研究来比较ERalpha反应。结果：碘乙酸（IAA）、氯乙腈（CAN）和溴乙腈（BAN）在hERalpha上显示出强烈的雌激素活性（最大诱导率分别为108.7%、50.3%和54.7%），而IAA强烈抑制了17β-雌二醇（E2）在zERalpha中诱导的雌激素活性（最大浓度下诱导率为59.8%）。氯乙酰胺（CAM）和溴乙酰胺（BAM）在zERalpha中也显示出强烈的抗雌激素效应（最大浓度下诱导率分别为48.1%和50.8%）。这些不同的内分泌干扰模式通过Pearson相关性和基于距离的分析进行了全面评估。观察到两种ERalpha的雌激素反应存在明显差异，而抗雌激素活性模式无法建立。一些DBPs作为hERalpha激动剂强烈诱导雌激素内分泌干扰，而其他则作为zERalpha拮抗剂抑制雌激素活性。主坐标分析（PCoA）显示雌激素和抗雌激素反应的相关系数相似。计算分析和报告基因检测获得了可重复的结果。结论：总体而言，DBPs对人类和斑马鱼的影响强调了控制其雌激素活性响应差异的重要性，包括水质监测和内分泌干扰，因为DBPs具有物种特异性的配体-受体相互作用。
